proposed_comments.body:
### Timed-out Foundry CLI commands can outlive their timeout

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `src/common/LanguageModelProvider/FoundryLocal/FoundryClient.cs` — `RunFoundryJsonAsync` and `StartDaemonAsync`.

**Problem:** Both methods start a `foundry` process and await it with a cancellation timeout. When the read/exit wait is cancelled, the exception path returns after disposing the `Process` wrapper, but does not stop the native CLI process. A CLI command that stalls beyond the configured 10- or 30-second limit can therefore continue running after the provider reports failure.

**Why it matters:** Repeated availability, daemon-discovery, or cache lookups can start further CLI commands while an earlier timed-out command remains alive, defeating the intended time bounds and potentially accumulating background processes.

**Suggested change:** Give each launched CLI process explicit timeout cleanup: on cancellation, check whether it has exited and terminate/reap the CLI process before returning, handling the exit race. Preserve normal completion behavior, and avoid killing a daemon that `foundry server start` has already detached.

**Verification:** On the pinned head, both timeout awaits flow to catch-and-return paths with no process termination. A local .NET `Process.Dispose()` probe confirmed the child process remained alive until explicitly stopped. No PowerToys build or Foundry integration run was performed; verify timeout and normal-exit paths for both commands, including that a successful server start leaves its daemon running.
proposed_comments.title: Stop timed-out Foundry CLI processes
